submission.text: The full text of the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR), the Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul (RFO), and Defense Federal Acquisition Regulations Supplement (DFARS) can be accessed on the internet at www.acquisition.gov. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; quotes are being requested and a written solicitation will not be issued. • Set-Aside: This procurement is 100% set-aside for Women-Owned Small Business (WOSB) • NAICS Code: 541810 (Advertising Agencies) • Small Business Size Standard: $25.5 Million • Federal Product/Service Code: R701 • Award Type: Firm-Fixed-Price 2. SUBMISSION DEADLINES • Questions Due: THURSDAY, 30 JULY 2026 at 7:00 am (MST) • Answers Posted: THURSDAY, 6 AUG 2026 FRIDAY, 7 AUG 2026 • Solicitation Closes (Quotes Due): THURSDAY, 20 AUG 2026 at 7:00 am (MST) FRIDAY, 21 AUG 2026 at 7:00 am (MDT) All quotes and questions must be received electronically by email to: delache.n.jnobaptiste.civ@army.mil. 3. CONTRACT LINE ITEM NUMBERS (CLINs) Offerors must complete the following pricing table. The proposed price must be fully burdened and all-inclusive of all labor, media/ad spend, software licenses, administrative costs, and reporting required to fully execute the PWS. No separate onboarding or setup

Neither vendor responded to the request. To prevent a critical lapse in coverage for this mission-essential data center infrastructure, the Government expanded its market research to the Open Market. This effort identified PivIT Global as a technically capable, authorized reseller. To ensure the Government obtains the best value and provides a fair opportunity to all qualified sources, the final solicitation will be posted on SAM.gov as an Open Market, Unrestricted competition using the commercial procedures of FAR Part 12. This approach removes the restrictive SEWP small business constraints, inviting any capable, authorized third-party maintenance provider in the commercial market to compete. 7. Over the past several years, Knowledge Management has expanded its portfolio to provide IT solutions and services to CDC’s Centers Institutes and Offices (C/I/Os) as well as the United States Department of Transportation (USDOT), the National Oceanographic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC), and the Minority Business Development Agency (MBDA). The Government aims to transform the DGIB ecosystem into a secure, scalable, cloud-based enterprise platform. This platform will facilitate comprehensive claims processing, optimize automation where feasible, lessen dependence on outdated systems, improve the experiences of both Veterans and employees, and offer the adaptability needed for future legislative, policy, and technological shifts. Through this Request for Information (RFI), the VA is seeking insights from industry on the most effective technical and acquisition strategies to reach this goal. This includes suggestions on solution architecture, implementation plans, and contract frameworks. This is an RFI issued for conducting market research and for eliciting industry input as to the Government’s requirement for DGIB and Education Services Automation and Modernization. The system currently holds an active Authority to Operate (ATO) in a vendor-managed AWS GovCloud environment. VBA is conducting market research to modernize, migrate, and enhance the DGIB platform in alignment with VA's cloud-first strategy and broader enterprise modernization goals. VBA is exploring five primary capability areas, described in the Requirement section below, and is seeking industry input to inform its evaluation of potential approaches. Current Systems The DGIB ecosystem consists of legacy systems slated for replacement and modern systems built to replace them but not yet at full operational capability. DGIB processes more than $12 billion in education benefits annually. Automation rates vary by chapter and have improved meaningfully year-over-year, with an overall automation rate of approximately 60% across all benefit chapters. Automated claims are resolved in approximately one day across all chapters, compared to 9.5–18.7 days for manually adjudicated claims, depending on chapter. Enrollment Manager (EM) EM is an Education Service web-based system used by schools and training facilities to certify enrollments and report changes for Veterans and other eligible beneficiaries receiving VA education benefits. EM streamlines communication between educational institutions and VA by enabling electronic submission of enrollment certifications for all EDU benefits and timely delivery of education benefits. ip_data_security.text: n, partial automation, or manual adjudication by a Veteran Claims Examiner (VCE). Automation levels for claims are defined as: Automated Claim: A claim received, processed and authorized by automated adjudication without any human intervention. Partially Automated Claim: A claim where automation initiates the claim, applies processing rules, but must be authorized manually (by a human). Manual Claim: A claim received or generated outside of DGIB (EM or MEB) and created and authorized by manual adjudication. The current DGIB operating environment relies on a Managed Service Vendor (MSV) responsible for application development, infrastructure hosting, and operations and maintenance across a complex, mature platform that includes 700+ repositories, 50+ databases (Oracle 19C, PostgreSQL 14, Amazon Redshift, DynamoDB), and extensive CI/CD infrastructure. Other current systems configuration includes: 76 EC2 compute instances (Windows Server and Red Hat Enterprise Linux), 590+ compiled software artifacts , 30+ S3 object storage buckets and 90+ vendor, open-source, and hardware licenses. The system currently holds an active Authority to Operate (ATO) in a vendor-managed AWS GovCloud environment. entity_geography.text: L Developer-Modeler, Oracle Spatial; Oracle Web Application Development tools including the MOD PLSQL Toolkit, Application Express (APEX) kit, HTML5, JavaScript, XML, KML, Microsoft Excel, Microsoft Access and NMEA message formats. Due to design linkages to GIS information environments, proficiency in use and development of applications for Google/Earth including the decoding, storage, and retrieval of waterborne vessel AIS movement data in the Oracle environment stated above will be required. Familiarity with proficiency in support of cloud residency of application and transfer\interface protocols and triggers to access and activate cloud resident applications will also be of value for efficient execution of assigned work. All triggers, interface procedures and packages developed for working with and handling data or databases within the environment as described and required by\for USACE shall be fully verified as to functionality and documented for purposes of efficient follow-on or inheriting assignment for maintenance or upgrade by any designated or supporting technical programmers and systems administrators. It should be understood that the latter requirement may entail more or supplemental documentation than would accompany the primary documentation of the contractor’s core deve

eeds regarding system application internal to USACE or for allowances needed for a system that would allow some level of defined capabilities for public access or higher levels of data aggregation implemented at a later time. Respective to internal usage, NNOMPEAS has been definitively assessed as requiring at a minimum an IL4-level environment subject to containment and protections for data and information that falls under classification as CUI (controlled unclassified information). While an IL4-level environment is considered the minimum and hence required environment specification, currently the system is not assessed, presently or foreseeably, as requiring support for a higher impact level (IL) rating. Required Competencies and Qualifications - In regard to the technical nature of work as set forth in items or deliverables as described in Section 3 herein, the Contractor must have and demonstrate in any respective proposal strong working knowledge and skills in the analytical areas of deep-draft waterborne transportation economics; ideally both as applied in the private sector and by the USACE, naval architecture, and vessel management or evaluation of related management practices to acceptably or more fully understand potential applications of the system and critical needs f

rmation, and maritime databases or data sources generally available in the public realm or from the private non-governmental and commercial maritime sector(s). Subject to practical application of such knowledge and skills as generally described, modifications or enhancements needed under the performance work statement herein for the NNOMPEAS system are described as follows: 3-1 -- Migration to update(s) beyond the current version of Oracle (currently 19c base) and current or supporting versions of Oracle APEX -- As described above, the USACE Oracle platform is currently fully compatible to operation under Oracle version(s) 19c and foreseeably 26AI. Development of Computerized Methods & Procedures for NNOMPEAS System Operation 1. Introduction and Background The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Institute for Water Resources (IWR) has been tasked by the USACE to develop and maintain a centralized computer-based system to tabulate waterborne transportation cost structures for coastal deep-draft waterway system projects under Federal sponsorship and jurisdiction of USACE. Waterborne transportation cost structures

or Water Resources (IWR) has been tasked by the USACE to develop and maintain a centralized computer-based system to tabulate waterborne transportation cost structures for coastal deep-draft waterway system projects under Federal sponsorship and jurisdiction of USACE. Waterborne transportation cost structures and the differentials therein as derived from or associated with waterway project or plan alternatives serve as the primary basis for estimation of economic benefit(s) and indication(s) for return on investment (ROI) of waterway improvement and maintenance projects. Under initial and subsequent efforts for development, the emphasis of output for system development was (and continues to be) the compilation of information and data inputs in turn applied for estimation of waterborne transportation costs for deep-draft ocean-going and coastwise carriers conveying foreign (i.e., imports and exports) and domestic trade serving coastal deep-draft harbors of the United States. Notably, the array of harbors and waterway systems is limited to harbors and locations for which the Corp’s Waterborne Commerce Statistics Center (WCSC) compiles waterway vessel and cargo or commodity movement or traffic data and information. With the development of other separate database efforts within and exte

Corp’s Waterborne Commerce Statistics Center (WCSC) compiles waterway vessel and cargo or commodity movement or traffic data and information. With the development of other separate database efforts within and external to USACE the intent is to develop the capability to compile vessel operations data and information and tabulate the nature and extent of waterway use and transportation or operational efficiencies incurred by commercial vessels. This information in turn can be combined with eventual application to relevant program operation & maintenance (O&M) and new work project planning data and information assembled within the framework of requirements for life-cycle cost evaluation with comparability to general program management objectives of the Corps for measurement of applicable return on investment (ROI). In addition, while the emphasis of system development will be for eventual capacity for evaluation of operation and maintenance (O&M) of coastal deep-draft waterways, the logic and procedures for life-cycle project economic benefit and cost evaluation(s) are to be comparable with established guidance and USACE analytical procedures applied for navigation project evaluations whether for planning or new work as well as evaluation of significant O&M efforts. n Foreign Procurements-Notice and Representation (Jun 2020) (a) Deﬁnitions. As used in this provision- Foreign person means any person other than a United States person. Speciﬁed Federal procurement payment means any payment made pursuant to a contract with a foreign contracting party that is for goods, manufactured or produced, or services provided in a foreign country that is not a party to an international procurement agreement with the United States. For purposes of the prior sentence, a foreign country does not include an outlying area of the United States. United States person as deﬁned in 26 U.S.C. 7701(a)(30) means (1) A citizen or resident of the United States; (2) A domestic partnership; (3) A domestic corporation; (4) Any estate (other than a foreign estate, within the meaning of 26 U.S.C. 701(a)(31)); and (5) Any trust if- (i) A court within the United States is able to exercise primary supervision over the administration of the trust; and (ii) One or more United States persons have the authority to control all substantial decisions of the trust. (b) Unless exempted, there is a 2 percent tax of the amount of a speciﬁed Federal procurement payment on any foreign person receiving such payment. See 26 U.S.C. 5000C and its implementing regulations at 26 CFR 1.5000C-1 through 1

deliverables_scope.text: Wilmington, DE 19804. This Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) is issued to competitively obtain a fully engineered, code‑compliant, and operational turnkey system solution that optimizes vertical cube utilization, enhances equipment security, and meets best practice storage and safety criteria. The design and installation must promote safety, ergonomics, and operational efficiency for Army National Guard personnel. Problem Statement DE ARNG requires an industrial organizational storage solution that: Supports military-grade equipment storage and accountability. Offers long-term structural stability and compliance with UFC 4-440-01 warehouse requirements. Delivers secure enclosures meeting AR 735-5 physical security requirements. Integrates shelving systems suitable for ergonomic manual loading. Complements and leverages its newly constructed building. Available documents include a 65-percent design specification and an as-built drawing set (controlled access for vetted contractors). Desired System Attributes and Capabilities DE ARNG is interested in innovative commercial products/services/solutions roughly comparable to those in the 65-percent design specification or better. Submission Process Site Visit: Non-mandatory site visit is at 2:00 PM ET Tuesday 18 Aug 2026 at the facility. Provid

certifications_partner.text: ===== FILE: files/Notice_of_Intent_Sole_Source_SANS-135419.docx ===== NOTICE OF INTENT TO AWARD A SOLE SOURCE CONTRACT The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) intends to award a Sole Source firm-fixed price commercial Purchase Order (PO) to the Escal Institute of Advanced Technologies, Inc., dba SANS Institute (“SANS”), is the sole provider of SANS training and Global Information Assurance Certification (“GIAC”) Certifications in accordance with the authority under FAR RFO Part 6.302-1, Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements. The NAICS Code for this action is 611420 – Computer Training. This acquisition is being conducted using simplified acquisition procedures in accordance with FAR RFO Part 12 for the acquisition of commercial products and commercial services. The FDA Office of Criminal Investigations (OCI), Digital Forensics Program (DFP) requires the following commercially available supplies and services from the SANS Institute to support continuing education and professional certi

This acquisition is being conducted using simplified acquisition procedures in accordance with FAR RFO Part 12 for the acquisition of commercial products and commercial services. The FDA Office of Criminal Investigations (OCI), Digital Forensics Program (DFP) requires the following commercially available supplies and services from the SANS Institute to support continuing education and professional certification for federal digital forensics personnel: • SANS Institute Universal Training Vouchers, each redeemable SANS long-course enrollment across any eligible training modality (Live In-Person, Live Online, or OnDemand). • Global Information Assurance Certification (GIAC) examination attempts, bundled with or issued in conjunction with each training voucher, valid for a minimum of twelve (12) months from course completion or voucher activation. All SANS courseware and GIAC Certification exams are copyright protected. SANS updates its curriculum multiple times per year to address the latest industry trends and in conjunction with GIAC exams.
